SplitAlignerR

SplitAlignerR aligns gene-tree branches to species-tree coordinates. The C++17 SplitAlignerFast backend maps exact taxon bitsets through C ABI 2. A separate pure R implementation independently recomputes the Catnip10 graph-oracle benchmark. The package checks branch-length tokens before using them as numeric evidence.

For everyday use, start with align_branches(). It uses the split-based Fast backend for both free and fixed inputs. Setting mode = "fixed" does not switch algorithms. Choose align_fixed_topology() explicitly if you want the independent graph path for fixed-topology data. The Catnip10 oracle is a separate validation tool; you do not need to select an algorithm to run it.

In the manuscript’s current numbering, reference truth is Algorithm S1, the Perl workflow is S2, the Fast mapper used by align_branches() is S3, and align_fixed_topology() is S4. Older software records and filenames retain their original identifiers: S3 for reference truth and S2 for the Fast-backed R result. Those identifiers do not select a different algorithm.

v0.1.0 is the immutable Pro-RECERT-certified release. The default branch is the post-release development line. The Fast-backed prerelease has package version 0.1.0.9015 and is not covered by the v0.1.0 RECERT decision. The frozen v0.1.0-rc1, v0.1.0-rc2, and v0.1.0-rc3 tags are retained as historical release candidates.

Documentation site: https://wujiaqi06.github.io/SplitAlignerR/

Installation 

# install.packages("remotes")

# Stable, Pro-RECERT-certified release:
remotes::install_github("wujiaqi06/SplitAlignerR@v0.1.0")

# Fast-backed prerelease
remotes::install_github("wujiaqi06/SplitAlignerR@v0.1.0.9015")

Minimal Example 

library(SplitAlignerR)

catnip10_expected()
catnip10_summary_counts()
validate_catnip10_oracle()

# Independently rebuild all Catnip10 graph states in pure R.
rebuilt <- recompute_catnip10_oracle("global")
identical(rebuilt$matrix, catnip10_matrix("global"))

# Inspect the compiled core and its numeric input policy.
splitaligner_core_info()
validate_branch_length_tokens(c("0", "1e-8", "NaN", "1e9999"))

# Parse and canonicalize a reference tree in the C++ core.
validate_species_tree("((A:1,B:1),(C:1,D:1));")

# Align empirical trees. State and finite numeric evidence stay separate.
species <- "((A:1,B:1):1,(C:1,D:1):1);"
genes <- c(
  concordant = "((A:1,B:1):1,(C:1,D:1):1);",
  discordant = "((A:1,C:1):1,(B:1,D:1):1);",
  marker = "((A:NaN,B:1):1,(C:1,D:1):1);"
)
aligned <- align_branches(species, genes, mode = "free")
aligned$state_matrix
aligned$numeric_matrix

Fast-backed development package

Build the prerelease with a C++17 compiler and the Rcpp, ape and digest packages. Install this prerelease using R CMD INSTALL SplitAlignerR_0.1.0.9015.tar.gz. Use splitaligner_core_info() to inspect the active backend and source version.

The mapper uses exact taxon bitsets. It caches coverage projections within an alignment while preserving the R result’s branch order, source indices and fusion memberships. The fixed and free outputs retain separate graph states and numeric evidence. Pair them with pair_alignment_results() to produce the finalized matrix. Full result objects include per-cell provenance ledgers.

Projected split text in these ledgers is stored compactly and rendered on request. It remains a character column: selecting a few records does not expand every split in the panel. Use the package’s result writer or saveRDS(result, file, version = 3) to retain compact storage. Reading such a file requires SplitAlignerR 0.1.0.9014 or later. To save ordinary character columns for older installations, use saveRDS(result, file, version = 2); expanding the strings can increase memory use and file size. Operations that request a full character buffer or edit the text column can also expand it. For panels larger than available memory, use the batched disk interface below.

The result includes its per-branch Support table and the labeled reference tree in aligned$support_table and aligned$support_newick. To export the pair into a new directory, call write_branch_support(aligned, "support").

Fixed-topology alignment with Algorithm S4

For an explicit alternative to the default split mapper, when each gene tree has the topology of the reference restricted to that gene’s taxa, use:

fixed <- align_fixed_topology(
  "((A,B),C);",
  c(full = "(C:4,(B:2,A:1):3);", reduced = "(B:5,C:4);"),
  reference_semantics = "unrooted",
  gene_semantics = "unrooted"
)
fixed$reference_state_matrix # S3 states for every input gene's retained taxa
fixed$numeric_matrix         # Successful genes: original and fusion columns
fixed$observation_ledger     # Actual measurements and their input-edge sources
fixed$component_observations # Includes components absent from the input
fixed$fusion_ledger          # Construction and sources of each fusion-column value
fixed$gene_outcomes          # Successes and skipped genes, with reasons

S4 carries original branch members through graph pruning and contraction, then matches labeled tree structures before reading gene lengths. It does not call the Fast split mapper. A topology mismatch skips that gene and records its ID and reason; it does not become NA_topo. Other invalid inputs still raise errors. Check fixed$metadata$n_input, n_success and n_skipped_topology before using a result. If every gene is skipped, the result contains the full log and zero-row numeric matrices.

Reference identity and input measurements are separate. With reference_semantics = "rooted", S4 preserves the original reference root and ancestral stem exactly as S3 does. Gene trees still default to gene_semantics = "unrooted". If forgetting the root combines two reference components into one observed edge, its length is recorded once as a joint observation; it is never copied or divided into two original-branch values. An ancestral stem absent from the gene input remains in reference truth but has no measurement. This is distinct from an input edge whose length is missing. Use gene_semantics = "reference_rooted" only for inputs explicitly declared to preserve the reference root and its structure; a root-length annotation does not create a missing edge. The declaration does not establish that a model can estimate each root-adjacent length independently.

reference_state_matrix has all input rows and only observed, NA_struct and NA_fuse; observed describes reference identity, not empirical recovery. primitive_matrix, fusion_matrix and their combined numeric_matrix have successful genes only, in input order. Reference components and deletion-fusion columns keep their S3 definitions. Joint observations caused by input normalization are kept separately and do not create deletion fusions or change Support. primitive_observation_matrix reports individual, joint or unrepresented correspondence, alongside NA_struct for deleted originals.

The default fusion_view = "whole" constructs values only from complete reference components and complete available observation units. "direct" retains a value only when the complete target corresponds to one normalized observation unit, even when its reference state is decomposable. Such a unit can itself sum multiple input edges when an unrooted display root is suppressed; its provenance records single_input_edge or input_edge_sum. Sources are counted once per target value. Different target columns can share sources and are not independent measurements. Input-edge IDs and hashes are provenance, not portable identities.

This candidate introduces result schema s4-observation-v1, without the old ambiguous state_matrix and component_ledger aliases. The old tree_semantics = "unrooted" argument is a deprecated alias and cannot be mixed with the new arguments. The old rooted spelling raises a migration error: choose the two new semantics explicitly, since the former rooted/MRCA result used a different reference definition. Historical results are unchanged.

This entry returns a separate splitaligner_fixed_result; read its matrices and ledgers directly. Existing support, paired, exchange and disk-panel accessors accept the S2 result type, not this type. S4 retains ordinary per-cell source tables and assembles the full result in memory. Reduced temporary assembly allocations do not make it disk-backed; large provenance-rich results can still require substantial memory. The batched disk interface applies to align_branches(), not align_fixed_topology(). Version 0.1.0.9015 is a development prerelease.

Reference truth tables, including rooted trees

To ask what happens to the original branches when taxa are removed, supply only the reference tree and retained taxa. No empirical gene tree is needed:

truth <- reference_truth(
  "((A:1,B:2):3,C:4);",
  list(full = c("A", "B", "C"), without_C = c("A", "B"),
       only_A = "A", empty = character(0)),
  tree_semantics = "rooted"
)
truth$state_matrix       # observed / NA_struct / NA_fuse on original branches
truth$original_matrix    # Separately retained original-branch lengths
truth$fusion_matrix      # Expected lengths in shared fusion coordinates
truth$component_ledger   # Complete original members and reference-edge sources

This S3 entry preserves the original root and the path to the retained taxa. The original root is exempt from degree-two contraction. Its convention matches the historical rooted benchmark, including the root-to-MRCA stem. S4 uses the same reference identity and separately records which components its gene input can measure. Missing input representation does not change S3 truth.

In a truth table, observed means that an original reference branch remains separately represented; it does not assert recovery in a gene tree. Expected lengths come only from the reference. If a required reference length is missing, the expected total stays missing. States and complete fusion membership still remain available. fusion_view = "whole" and "direct" follow the same complete- component rule as the mapping outputs, with reference sources clearly labeled.

An empty retained set has no edges. A single retained taxon keeps its original root-to-tip path in rooted mode; zero or one retained taxon has no edges in unrooted mode. The existing recompute_catnip10_oracle() entry and frozen Catnip10 data are unchanged. These truth tools are optional; ordinary mapping still starts with align_branches() and the split-based Fast default.

Working with large gene collections (0.1.0.9006)

Start with a reference tree and two files containing one named gene tree per line. In paired mode, use the same gene IDs in the same order in both files. Choose a new directory on a disk with space for the results.

panel <- align_panel_to_disk("speciesTree302.nwk", "free.2275genes.nwk",
                            "mammal-panel", mode = "paired",
                            fixed_file = "fix.2275genes.nwk", batch_size = 32L)
read_panel_matrix(panel, "paired_free", genes = c("AASDH", "ABCA1"),
                  branches = c("B1", "B2"))
patterns <- panel_fusion_patterns(panel)
read_panel_groups(panel, genes = "ABCA12")

The first pass records each fusion pattern by its original reference branches and writes per-gene evidence to disk. The second pass reads the batches for the genes you request. A pattern discovered in the last batch is available in the same column for any selection. To see whether a pattern formed and was recovered, pass composite IDs to read_panel_fusions() and request field = "recovery_status". For a temporary run, pass tempfile("mammal-") as the output directory and keep the returned path until you finish reading.

The default fusion view uses complete current components. A group formed in a later batch can receive a sum in an earlier gene. Use read_panel_fusion_cells(panel, genes, patterns) for the source edges of each selected value, or fusion_view = "direct" when creating a panel for single-edge measurements. Older panels keep their recorded direct values.

To export a whole matrix, stream the second pass to a new TSV file. Each row contains one gene, with the same reference and fusion columns throughout.

export_panel_matrix(panel, "free-lengths.tsv", "free_length", include_fusions = TRUE)

Each new panel also writes support.tsv and support.nwk under free/ or fixed/. In paired mode, open free/support.nwk for the free-tree Support percentages and fixed/support.nwk for the fixed-tree ones. The writer sums each branch’s eligible and recovered gene counts across all batches before computing its label.

The panel stores primitive lengths and states, paired tokens where requested, and per-gene fusion records. For full per-cell provenance, use align_branches() on the genes of interest. Reduce batch_size for wider reference trees. The reference, one batch, the gene and fusion indexes, and the slice you request need to fit in memory.

Fusion members and their shared split

For each gene, missing taxa can cause two or more reference branches to project onto one split. Each primitive member keeps NA_fuse in its own cell. Inspect the group once to find its length or see why the length is unavailable:

species <- "((A,B),C,(D,(E,F)));"
genes <- c(g1 = "((A,B):0.31,D,(E,F):0.17);",
           g2 = "((A,B):0.26,E,(D,F));",
           g3 = "((A,D),B,(E,F):0.23);")
free <- align_branches(species, genes, mode = "free")
groups <- free_fusion_groups(free)
groups[, c("gene_id", "primitive_members", "projected_split", "recovery_status",
           "graph_class", "final_token")]

For these three genes, the same two reference branches form a fusion group. The shared split is present at length 0.31 in g1 and 0.26 in g2. The g3 tree lacks the split, so its group token is NA_fuse_topo. Both members still carry NA_fuse in all three genes. A displayed group with no finite length has graph class Mapped and a literal NA value. An unresolved free tree can also lack the split.

Choose the counting unit when tabulating the five outcomes.

count_free_topology(free, unit = "primitive")
count_free_topology(free, unit = "coordinate")

Each row satisfies Total = Mapped + NA_struct + NA_fuse + NA_topo + NA_fuse_topo. For g3, the absent shared split contributes two to NA_fuse_topo in primitive accounting (Total = 9) and one in coordinate accounting (Total = 8). Mapped counts displayed singletons, including those with missing lengths. Both units count each structurally lost primitive once. The accounting weights leave the two primitive cells for the absent split labeled NA_fuse.

Primitive branch recovery uses only eligible reference branches. In g3, each member of the absent group is already NA_fuse in the reference layer and has no independent observation in the free tree. Each therefore contributes zero to both the recovery numerator and its denominator. The group still appears once in the group table.

The default pair_alignment_results(fixed, free) exposes the same group table as $free_fusion_groups. Use rule = "legacy" for frozen paired schema 1.0.0 matrices, including their historical residual NA tokens.

Use export_splitaligner_exchange() for fixed-mode exchange and validate_splitaligner_exchange() to verify an exchange object’s structure and seals. See ?splitaligner_exchange for its reference-tree requirements.

V1 Scope

The certified V1 release combines the production mapper with the independent Catnip10 benchmark track. It includes:

  • catnip10_expected() / catnip10_matrix() for the wide primitive-coordinate oracle matrix;
  • catnip10_summary_counts() for per-regime status accounting;
  • catnip10_fusion_groups() for graph-oracle fused-coordinate membership;
  • validate_catnip10_oracle() for deterministic benchmark sanity checks;
  • recompute_catnip10_oracle() for an independent pure R reconstruction of every Catnip10 primitive state and fusion group;
  • validate_branch_length_tokens() for C++ whole-token and finite-range numeric validation;
  • validate_species_tree() for C++ Newick parsing, diagnostics, and canonical unrooted primitive coordinates;
  • align_branches() for C++ graph-first primitive classification, empirical split recovery, composite provenance, and finite numeric evidence;
  • coordinate_provenance() and summary() for member-set and run-level inspection;
  • save_splitaligner_result() / read_splitaligner_result() for checked, lossless result persistence;
  • pair_alignment_results() for a separate fixed/free finalized-output layer that preserves literal NA, summarizes it as residual_NA, and never changes the single-tree graph ledger;
  • splitaligner_core_info() for core, schema, and numeric-policy metadata;
  • catnip10_oracle, the bundled data object containing the frozen species tree, branch-label crosswalk, per-cell oracle states, and fusion groups.

The Catnip10 benchmark is discordance-free by design. It exercises the graph-defined observed, NA_fuse, and NA_struct ledger states under taxon pruning. NA_topo is not expected in this benchmark because empirical gene-tree discordance is outside the Catnip10 oracle fixture.

Release and audit boundary

The production mapper lives in the C++ core. R converts inputs and wraps the result; the Catnip10 Oracle remains a separate pure R node-edge implementation that never calls the core or uses projected splits for structural states.

The legacy contract field finalized_perl_matrices_are_authoritative is intentionally named. Here, Perl refers to the frozen SplitAligner reference implementation; SplitAlignerR does not require Perl at runtime.

The V1 tests reproduce all 272 frozen Catnip10 primitive cells and all 19 fusion events, and include explicit discordance and unavailable numeric-evidence toys. The immutable v0.1.0 source passed independent Pro RECERT; changes on the default development branch do not inherit that certification. The scientific, numeric, provenance, and paired-bookkeeping boundaries are recorded in inst/spec/V1_SCIENTIFIC_CONTRACT.md.

See vignette("quick-start", package = "SplitAlignerR") for the layered result model, batch input forms, diagnostics, provenance lookup, and save/reload flow.
